version.changelog:
Initial release of alibabacloud-cfw-internet-firewall-protect.

- Manage Cloud Firewall public IP protection on Alibaba Cloud, supporting enable/disable for individual or bulk assets.
- Supports asset protection queries, auto-protection configuration, and multi-account operations with member-uid.
- Provides flexible filtering by IP, region, resource type, and IPv4/IPv6, plus condition-based multi-step workflows.
- Includes robust CLI environment validation and permission troubleshooting guidance.
- Compatible with aliyun CLI >= 3.3.3 (with CFW plugin) and several execution engines.

llm.summary: This skill has a legitimate firewall-management purpose, but it can broaden narrow requests into account-wide firewall changes and uses risky CLI installation/update guidance.

dimensions.detail: The skill requires local Alibaba Cloud CLI credentials and RAM permissions for firewall read/write APIs, including account-wide and member-account operations. That authority is purpose-aligned but broad, and the unsafe widening rules make it under-scoped for narrow requests.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: validate-cli.sh does not execute a remote installer itself, but it repeatedly recommends curl -fsSL https://aliyuncli.alicdn.com/setup.sh | bash, enables global auto plugin install, and recommends aliyun plugin update without pinning or integrity verification.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to continue execution when zero assets match and to fall back to broader dimensions or enable-all --yes; it also conflicts with its own explicit-confirmation language by treating non-interactive --yes as confirmation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No backdoor or hidden system persistence was found, but the skill changes persistent cloud firewall state, persistent auto-protection configuration, and local CLI/plugin settings such as auto-plugin-install and plugin updates.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Managing Alibaba Cloud Firewall public-IP protection is coherent with the skill purpose, but the artifacts include high-impact write operations such as enable-all, disable-all, and auto-protection modification, plus instructions that can expand beyond the user's selected assets.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. Use it only with tightly scoped RAM permissions, avoid running the curl-to-bash installer guidance, do not allow zero-match requests to broaden automatically, and require an explicit preview and confirmation for the exact account, filters, and final asset set before any enable-all, disable-all, or auto-protection change.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: Verified in SKILL.md: zero-match conditional workflows are told to broaden scope and eventually call enable-all --yes, which is not a safe or expected interpretation of a narrow user filter.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Verified in SKILL.md: enable-all --yes is a documented fallback when no assets match, creating account-wide impact without a fresh user-approved scope.
[SSD-4] unexpected: Verified in SKILL.md: the scope-expansion behavior is real and materially concerning for firewall state changes, though it is disclosed rather than hidden.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Verified in SKILL.md: explicit confirmation is required in one section, while another says non-interactive --yes is implicit confirmation and commands must run unconditionally.
[SC2] unexpected: Verified in validate-cli.sh: the script prints curl-to-bash installation guidance. CLI setup guidance is expected, but immediate execution of mutable remote code is not proportionate.
[TM2] unexpected: Verified in validate-cli.sh: the pipe-to-bash pattern appears in install and remediation text, not as automatic execution; this downgrades intent concern but leaves supply-chain risk.
[AE1] expected: The referenced scripts are present locally and were inspected, so the scanner's partial-inspection concern is not supported after review.
[SQP-3] expected: Hard-coded --Lang zh appears in API calls. This may affect usability and localization, but it is not a material security concern compared with the firewall mutation and install risks.
[T01] unexpected: Static scan's scope-broadening concern is supported by SKILL.md instructions around zero matches, mandatory Phase 2 execution, and non-interactive --yes.
[T03] unexpected: Static scan's remote-installer concern is supported as user-facing setup guidance, though the artifact does not automatically fetch and execute the installer.
[T08] unexpected: Static scan's plugin supply-chain concern is supported: the skill recommends global auto plugin install and updating all plugins rather than a pinned Cloud Firewall plugin.
[T09] unexpected: Verified in auto-protect.sh: parse failures can become an empty config and then be written back after merging requested keys, which could unintentionally alter existing auto-protection settings.
